outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each of the 141 markers represents one individual sample measurement (rhythmicity index vs. period), so individual data points are inherently displayed rather than only an average.

Each marker plots the mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter/cell line; only the averaged value and error bar are shown, with no overlay of the individual replicate data points behind each mean.
These are smoothed density (line) plots of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes; line/density plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.
Box plots are exempt from this check since they already convey distribution/spread, and in this panel individual sample points (colored dots per reporter) are additionally overlaid on the boxes.
Polar histograms display the distribution of phase-difference values over time/bins rather than a single averaged summary statistic, so overlaying individual points is not applicable/needed.
This is a polar histogram showing the distribution of subtype-averaged phase differences across bins; histogram-type plots are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.
This panel is an illustrative example of a single signal fit to a decaying sinusoidal model (a line plot/schematic), not an averaged summary across samples, so the check does not apply.

Each of the 117 markers is an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; the error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for that single sample rather than variability across averaged replicates, so the plotted markers already constitute individual data points.
